title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 205 (Compensation for revocation by principal, or renunciation by agent)

content.overview: Where there is an express or implied contract that the agency should be continued for any period of time, the principal must make compensation to the agent, or the agent to the principal, as the case may be, for any previous revocation or renunciation of the agency without sufficient cause.
content.glance: Fixed-term agency revoked or renounced without sufficient cause → compensating party must make compensation.
content.study: Where there is an express or implied contract that the agency should be continued for any period of time, the principal must make compensation to the agent, or the agent to the principal, as the case may be, for any previous revocation or renunciation of the agency without sufficient cause.

sections.heading: Contract for continuance
sections.body: Express or implied contract that agency should continue for a period of time.

sections.heading: Revocation or renunciation without sufficient cause
sections.body: Previous revocation by principal or renunciation by agent without sufficient cause.

sections.heading: Compensation
sections.body: Principal compensates agent, or agent compensates principal, as the case may be.

provisions.title: Compensation for revocation by principal, or renunciation by agent

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 205 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Find contract for continuance; test sufficient cause; apply compensation duty.

examTips: Fixed period + without sufficient cause = compensation.
